chapters.title: A light out of place
panels: At The Proving Ground, the evening lanterns glow above a courtyard of chess tables and wet stone.
Caretaker Mira finds one lantern lit before dusk. Nobody admits touching it.
Inside its glass is a folded slip: a drawing of the old archive door.
The archive door is locked, yet fresh chalk dust sits beside its keyhole.
A student remembers hearing a bicycle bell when the lantern first shone.
Mira compares the bell's time with the tea stall's closing note. Someone was early, not late.
On Sunday, the archive opens. Its ledgers are safe, but one page has been turned to a blank margin bearing a tiny blue dot.
chapters.bonus: The boss board reveals a second blue dot, tucked beneath the lantern's brass base.

chapters.title: Blue dots
panels: The blue dots match the ink used by the Ground's mapmaker, Dev.
Dev says his ink bottle has been missing since the first rain.
A receipt from the canteen bears the same blue mark, though no one ordered that item.
Mira learns the receipt was used as a bookmark, not a bill.
Its page number points to a register of donated books.
One book was returned by hand and entered as returned by post.
On Sunday, they open it. A pressed jasmine flower falls out, wrapped in a note addressed to someone who left years ago.
chapters.bonus: The bonus panel shows a pencilled route from the book shelf to the old clock.

chapters.title: The clock's quiet hour
panels: The old clock has been slow by seven minutes since the monsoon began.
That makes the bicycle bell and the tea stall note agree after all.
Dev remembers lending his ink to the clock repairer for a label.
The label is gone, but its outline remains on a small wooden box.
Mira finds the box empty except for a train ticket stub.
The ticket was never used. It was kept to remember an arrival instead.
On Sunday, the clock repairer admits the box held letters for a reunion. The last letter is missing.
chapters.bonus: Behind the clock face sits a paper bird folded from the missing letter's envelope.

chapters.title: A letter in plain sight
panels: The paper bird carries no name, only a sketch of the Ground's banyan tree.
At the tree, Mira finds a ribbon tied around a low branch.
The ribbon belongs to the annual welcome ceremony, held the next morning.
Dev checks the ceremony list. One guest's name was added in different ink.
The added guest is a retired teacher who helped start The Proving Ground.
She says the missing letter was hers, and she wanted it read aloud only after the welcome.
On Sunday, the letter is found beneath the podium. Its first line thanks a person no one remembers inviting.
chapters.bonus: The bonus panel shows a seat left empty beside the teacher's name card.

chapters.title: The empty seat
panels: Mira asks who was meant to sit in the empty place.
The retired teacher smiles: it was for the Ground's first caretaker, now living nearby.
The caretaker had quietly repaired the lantern before the ceremony.
He left the blue dots as a trail so the old group could find the letter together.
The turned ledger page was where they once planned this courtyard.
At tea, everyone adds a new note to that page: what they hope the Ground becomes next.
On Sunday, the lantern lights at dusk again. Beneath the new notes lies a fresh, unsigned invitation for tomorrow.
chapters.bonus: The boss board reveals its gentle request: bring one small puzzle to share.
